state:
Goal `tools-config`. Twelve of the configuration chapter's thirteen features have all their proofs. The one
left is `tools:config/mode`, and `bun nv proofs --verify --group tools:config` names only it. A tool feature
owes one example, one attack and one test (a Rust test or a `.nvst` case with a `covers:` marker counts).
A feature whose proof needs settings puts its own `nvs.toml` in the feature directory, and the runner hands
it over as `--config`, so run such a proof with `bun nv proofs --run --show --id '<feature>'`. A hostile case
with `// hostile: expect-refusal` passes on *any* diagnostic, a type error included, so check that the
refusal it prints is the one it attacks. Nothing is blocked.

items.text: **`tools:config/mode`** — owes examples, hostile, tests. `rule:testing/feature-proofs`. `docs/reference/tools/20-config.md:169`. A `covers:` marker on an existing `nvs-config` test of `[mode] default` and `ceiling` is the test. When the group check passes, close the goal: `bun nv verify --doc`, `bun nv owners --closes tools-config`, `bun nv playbook --closes tools-config`, then `DONE`.

backlog: `spawn script` of a file in a granted spawn directory that is not a program prints the file's text (PHP's inline-text rule). So `script.spawn` can read any file under its roots without `fs.read`. It is not checked whether this is intended. `rule:security/capability-declaration-is-one-table` owns capabilities.

A `[limits.hard]` value that does not parse makes every `Core\Config::set` of that key return `false`, even a value below the limit. This is safe, and pinned in `crates/nvs-config/tests/value.rs` (`an_incomparable_pair_exceeds`). `docs/reference/tools/20-config.md` § *Values and units* does not say so.
